title: Data entry domain basic statistics
question: When would you prefer the median over the mean to summarize a dataset, and what does standard deviation tell you that the mean alone doesn't?
idealAnswer:
The mean is sensitive to outliers, a few extreme values can pull it far from where most of the data actually sits

The median, the middle value when sorted, is robust to outliers and better represents a typical value in skewed distributions, e.g. income or house prices

The mean alone says nothing about spread, two datasets can have the same mean but very different variability

Standard deviation measures how spread out values are around the mean, a small standard deviation means values cluster tightly, a large one means they're spread widely

A strong answer gives a concrete example, e.g. average household income being skewed upward by a small number of very high earners, where the median is a better summary
